title: Equivariant smooth Galois alteration model before imposing degree conditions
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $B$ be a nonempty normal proper finite-type $e$-scheme which is a finite disjoint union of integral schemes and is geometrically reduced over $e$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $C_B\subseteq B$ be the support of an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. There are a finite extension $K/e$ [def-pc-field-extension], a finite group $G$ acting on $K$ by $e$-automorphisms, a smooth projective $K$-scheme $Y$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-kun-projective], and a projective surjective morphism $h:Y\to B$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The group $G$ acts on $Y$ by $e$-scheme automorphisms, $h$ is invariant, and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is equivariant. The extension $K^G/e$ is purely inseparable. The morphism $h$ sends every generic point of $Y$ to a generic point of $B$, with finite residue-field extension [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field]. The finite scheme quotient $q_G:Y\to Y/G$ exists and there is a dense open $U\subseteq B$, meeting every component, such that $(Y/G)\times_B U\to U$ is a finite universal homeomorphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. The quotient has orbit geometric fibres, has invariant structure sheaf, and is categorical for invariant morphisms. The reduced inverse image $(h^{-1}C_B)_{\rm red}$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor on $Y/K$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. This means that it is a reduced effective Cartier divisor with finitely many distinct integral components, and every intersection of $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth over $K$ of pure codimension $r$, including $r=0$, when the intersection is $Y$. All quotients by subgroups of $G$ also exist and are finite quotients with these orbit and invariant-sheaf properties. Projective over a field means a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space. No degree condition is imposed on $K/e$ or $h$. The empty divisor is allowed. Field-extension terminology and degrees are as in [def-pc-field-tower].

source.place: Expose X Lemma 2.2, printed pp.149--150, and 2.3 Step 2 through diagram (2.b), pp.150--151: finite-family form of the induced equivariant model. The common constants and group are obtained simultaneously before choosing any Sylow subgroup; for disconnected B use all its finitely many components, not separate prime-degree constant fields.

proof.text: Write $B=\coprod_{j=1}^n B_j$ using the given finite disjoint integral components. Apply the Galois component presentation to each $B_j$. It gives $e_{0j}/e$, a normal geometrically integral proper $e_{0j}$-scheme $X_j$, its finite group $H_j$, and $u_j:X_j\to B_j$. In particular $u_j$ is finite etale surjective and its geometric fibres are single $H_j$-orbits. The pullback of $C_B$ is an $H_j$-stable Cartier support $Z_j$. This also verifies the nowhere dense hypothesis: in an integral local domain a nonzero Cartier equation does not vanish at the generic point. The faithful semilinear action and geometric integrality are exactly the hypotheses of the nodal-tower input, not properties inferred merely from the notation $B_{e_{0j}}$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, p.150, geometric component and decomposition subgroup.

proof.text: For each $(X_j/e_{0j},H_j,Z_j)$ apply the equivariant marked plurinodal alteration. Denote its constants by $F_j$, its group by $J_j$, the surjection by $\rho_j:J_j\to H_j$, and its tower and marked closed sets by $T_{ji},Z_{ji}$. We obtain an equivariant projective generically finite surjection $a_j:T_{jd_j}\to X_j$, with $a_j^{-1}Z_j\subseteq Z_{jd_j}$. Over a dense open of $X_j$, every geometric fibre is one orbit under $N_j=\ker\rho_j$. Retain this orbit assertion when making the following birational modifications; it will control the full quotient, rather than only the degree of the alteration.

source.place: X 2.2 proof, p.149, application of Vidal 4.4.3.

proof.text: Resolve the tower by induction on $i$. The induction data are a smooth integral projective $F_j$-scheme $S_{j,i-1}$ with an equivariant projective birational map to $T_{j,i-1}$ and relative SNC boundary equal to the reduced preimage of $Z_{j,i-1}$. Start with $S_{j0}=\operatorname{Spec}F_j$ and empty boundary. Apply the one-curve resolution lemma to $f_{ji}:T_{ji}\to T_{j,i-1}$, $D=Z_{j,i-1}$, its marked sections and the already constructed base modification $S_{j,i-1}\to T_{j,i-1}$. Its conclusion resolves the fibre product and makes the composite back to $T_{ji}$ projective birational and surjective, giving $S_{ji}$ and precisely that induction datum with $i$ in place of $i-1$. The projectivity clause of the lemma applies because the preceding base is projective over $F_j$. At the top obtain $S_j=S_{jd_j}$, smooth integral projective over $F_j$, with equivariant birational $r_j:S_j\to T_{jd_j}$ and relative SNC boundary $E_j=(r_j^{-1}Z_{jd_j})_{\mathrm{red}}$. The lemma gives regular local rings and parameter equations for $E_j$. Length zero requires no resolution. Each modification induces equality of function fields; thus $a_jr_j$ remains dominant and generically finite.

source.place: X 2.2 proof, p.149 last paragraph--p.150, successive applications of Vidal 4.4.4.

proof.text: The reduced inverse image $D_j$ of $C_B$ in $S_j$ is a sub-divisor of $E_j$, not necessarily the whole marked boundary. Indeed, the composite $S_j\to B_j$ is dominant, so a local Cartier equation $c$ on $B_j$ pulls back to a nonzero element in the integral local ring of $S_j$. Off $E_j$ it is a unit, since its zero set is contained in $E_j$. At a point, write the boundary equations as distinct regular parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_r$. The cited regular-local UFD factorization gives $c=u\prod t_i^{a_i}$. Its reduced zero divisor is therefore cut out by $\prod_{a_i>0}t_i$. Globally these are a subset of the finitely many components of $E_j$. Their intersections are among the same smooth intersections, with the same codimensions, so $D_j$ is relative strict normal crossings. If $c$ is a unit, this subset is empty.

source.place: X 2.2 proof, p.149, the reduced inverse image is a subdivisor of the resolved marked boundary.

proof.text: Put $v_j=u_ja_jr_j:S_j\to B_j$. It is $J_j$-invariant since $u_j$ is $H_j$-invariant. At a geometric generic point of $B_j$, its lifts to $X_j$ form one $H_j$-orbit by the component presentation. Above each such lift, the geometric generic fibre of $a_jr_j$ is one $N_j$-orbit: the birational map $r_j$ induces equality of generic residue fields, and hence changes none of these geometric generic fibres. Given two points, first lift an element of $H_j$ carrying their images to one another along the surjection $\rho_j$, then use an element of $N_j$ in that fibre. Thus the whole geometric generic fibre of $v_j$ is one $J_j$-orbit. All generic residue extensions remain finite, and every generic point maps to the generic point of $B_j$.

source.place: X 2.2(iii) and X 2.3 Step 2, before (2.b): two-stage orbit argument.

proof.text: Apply common-field semilinear induction to the finite family $(F_j,J_j,S_j,v_j)$. Obtain one finite normal $K/e$, one finite group $G$ acting on $K$, and the induced schemes $Y_j$ with invariant maps to $B_j$. Set $Y=\coprod_jY_j$ and $h=\coprod_j(Y_j\to B_j)$. The induction lemma gives $K^G/e$ purely inseparable, single $G$-orbit geometric generic fibres, and finite residue extensions at every generic point. Every summand of $Y$ is a scalar twist of $S_j\times_{F_j}K$. Consequently $Y$ is smooth projective over $K$ and the reduced inverse image of $C_B$ is relative SNC: field extension preserves smoothness and all the intersection codimensions; any components that split are disjoint smooth components, so taking the reduced irreducible components gives the same condition. Twisting changes only the scalar structure. Finite disjoint unions preserve these properties (embed the finitely many projective summands in disjoint linear subspaces of one sufficiently large projective space). The map $h$ is surjective since each $v_j$ is surjective, the field base changes are surjective, and every coset family is nonempty.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, diagram (2.b); finite-family common normal constants and induced conjugate copies.

proof.text: The projective $K$-scheme $Y$ is also H-projective over $e$. The finite map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ is projective-bundle by the finite-morphism lemma; $\mathcal O$ is ample on the affine point (the section $1$ has affine nonvanishing locus), so the ample-base conversion makes it H-projective, and H-projective composition applies. Choose $i:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_e$. Since $B$ is proper over $e$, its diagonal is closed. The graph $Y\to Y\times_eB$ of $h$ is its base change, and $i\times\mathrm{id}_B$ is also a closed immersion by base change. Their composite embeds $Y$ into $\mathbf P^m_e\times_eB=\mathbf P^m_B$ over $B$. Thus $h$ is H-projective and therefore projective in the projective-bundle convention as well (use the free module $\mathcal O_B^{m+1}$). This establishes projectivity even though $B$ need not itself be projective over $e$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, projectivity of the induced alteration (graph verification).

proof.text: Apply finite quotient existence over $e$ to $Y$ and to every subgroup of $G$; the preceding projective embedding supplies its quasi-projective admission hypothesis. This gives all the finite categorical geometric quotients and their orbit and invariant-sheaf properties. In particular $h$ factors through $Q=Y/G$. For each $B_j$, choose a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A_j$. It is Noetherian by the component preparation. The morphism $h$ is projective and its generic fibre is zero-dimensional, since its finitely many generic residue extensions are finite. The projective-generically-finite lemma gives a nonempty open on which $h$ is finite; shrink this to a principal affine open in $\operatorname{Spec}A_j$. The quotient lemma then gives finiteness of $Q\to B$ there. These finitely many opens together meet every component. The generic fibre of $Q\to B_j$ is reduced, since invariant subrings of reduced rings are reduced, and has one geometric point by the orbit calculation. The radicial criterion applies also over the generic field: two distinct field-valued lifts would remain distinct over an algebraic closure, contradicting the one-point geometric fibre. Thus this generic morphism is radicial. Its reduced finite coordinate algebra has a single prime ideal, which is zero; being a finite-dimensional domain, it is a field, purely inseparable over $\kappa(B_j)$ by the same criterion.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, p.151, full quotient is generically radicial; retain actual finite quotients.

proof.text: Here is the dense-open radicial verification. On one of the preceding affine opens write $A\subseteq L=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and $Q=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ finite over $A$. Its generic algebra $R\otimes_A L$ is the purely inseparable field just found. Choose finitely many algebra generators $b_i$ of $R$. In characteristic $p>0$, choose a common $q=p^r$ with $b_i^q\in L$ in the generic algebra. Clear the finitely many denominators and annihilators of $b_i^q-a_i$ to obtain one nonzero $s\in A$ and $a_i\in A[1/s]$ such that $b_i^q=a_i$ in $R[1/s]$. In characteristic zero the generic field equals $L$ and the same argument uses $q=1$. For any field $M$ over $A[1/s]$, an $M$-valued point of $Q$ must send each $b_i$ to the unique possible root of $T^q-a_i$ in $M$. Hence there is at most one such point. The cited radicial criterion proves universal injectivity. Surjectivity holds because both $h$ and the quotient map are surjective. The integral-radicial-surjective lemma now makes this finite morphism a universal homeomorphism. Taking the union of these principal opens gives the required dense $U$ meeting every component. This last shrinking changes none of $Y,K,G,h$ or the boundary.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, p.151, verification of the universal-homeomorphism assertion on a dense open.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NK-dcd9fa8b4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Live item, not on side-live route-pivot-dropped.txt, still unsplit in live with the same statement; this is the 8th push. No dropped id is cited and the closure is clean. The new lem-sfb-admissible-finite-type-field-quotient states a true field-level admissible quotient for separated, locally finite-type schemes: finite categorical quotient, orbit fibres, sections are invariants, and finite over U when v^{-1}U is finite. The proof is invariant affine charts (Stacks 03JE/03BJ/03BL) plus Noether finiteness, and the finiteness-over-U clause holds without B Noetherian because invariants are integral and of finite type. It is the field case of dropped 1397/1939, not 1814, and asserts no projectivity. It differs from the NC 7dad copy because it is restricted to exactly the Step 8 use. No live existence node exists, and the item states quotient existence itself, so I accept it with a maintainer note. The other four new nodes are true and none restates an item clause: Galois component presentation (e'=H^0 separable, Galois closure, Stacks 0551/033C); Vidal 4.4.3 plurinodal alteration and 4.4.4 smooth-pair resolution step, matching ILO X 2.2 proof pp.149-150 (read); common normal-field contracted-product induction (compatible pairs, K^{Aut}/e purely inseparable, orbit transfer). Item Steps 1-9 checked: Step 3 induction datum matches the resolution conclusion (Z_i recursion); Step 4 c is a unit in A[1/T], then u∏t_i^{a_i}; Step 6 SNC survives scalar extension; Step 7 graph gives H-projectivity over proper B; Step 8 generic-fibre dimension 0, then finiteness over an open, then a reduced invariant generic algebra that is a purely inseparable field; Step 9 common q-th powers in R[1/s] give radicial, then finite+radicial+surjective gives a universal homeomorphism. Edge cases checked: empty C_B, dim 0, disconnected B, characteristic 0, inseparable K/e. Batch-5: def-trf SNC/projective-bundle definitions, trf finite-projective-bundle/h-projective conversion and composition, regular-local UFD factorization, and lem-fin-projective-generically-finite (via lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near) are all generic scheme theory outside the trace-formula and Poincare-duality proofs, so all accepted.
